prerequisites: Basic skills in: Mathematical analysis: derivatives, integrals, solving linear and quadratic equations, solving simple differential equations.
Euclidean geometry: elementary vector calculus, matrices.

learning_outcomes.text: The student who passes the exam will have acquired a strong understanding of the physical models used in mechanics and static electromagnetism, as well as a solid grasp of the related fundamental mathematical tools and the connection between theoretical and experimental physics
Ability to describe the motion in space of point-like objects or extended bodies using an appropriate vector formalism.
Ability to deduce the equations that describe the time evolution of the motion of objects subjected to external forces or actions.
Ability to understand and describe simple phenomena in electrostatics and magnetostatics.

syllabus_topics: Vector quantities and operations with vectors.
Universal gravitation and forces at a distance.

assessment_methods.method: Periodic assessment through exercises conducted in class
Assignment of exercises to be solved at home

assessment_rules: The student must demonstrate the ability to apply and critically follow the activities explained or carried out under the guidance of the instructor during the course. Problem-solving is the primary means of assessing knowledge. During the oral exam, the student must also demonstrate proficiency in using the correct terminology.
